Compute the perplexity of a transition tree

Source: R/likelihood.R
perplexity.Rd

perplexity() computes the perplexity of a fitted tree: the exponential of the negative mean log-likelihood per observed position, \(\exp(-\ell / n)\). It reads as an effective number of equally likely next states: a perplexity of \(k\) for \(k\) states means the tree predicts no better than chance, and a perplexity of 1 means every next state is predicted with certainty. Lower values indicate better prediction.

In-sample perplexity (without newdata) favors deep, lightly smoothed trees that reproduce the fitting data; held-out perplexity, computed on sequences not used for fitting, measures how well the tree generalizes. It returns a single number. tune_tree() uses cross-validated perplexity to choose a tree's settings.

Usage

perplexity(tree, newdata = NULL)

Arguments

tree

A transitiontrees object.

newdata

Sequences to score, in any form accepted by context_tree(). NULL (default) gives in-sample perplexity.

Value

A single number; NA when no position could be scored.

Conditions

transitiontrees_bad_input when tree is not a fitted tree or newdata has no usable sequence.

See also

model_fit(), score_sequences(), tune_tree(), plot_predictive().

Examples

tree <- context_tree(trajectories, max_depth = 2)
perplexity(tree)
#> [1] 2.310147
perplexity(tree, newdata = engagement)
#> [1] 2.137931
